title: Renal physiology

steps.tx: **Glomerular filtration rate** is determined by Starling forces across glomerular capillaries, where normal net ultrafiltration pressure of approximately 10 to 15 mmHg is driven by glomerular capillary hydrostatic pressure opposing plasma oncotic pressure and Bowman space hydrostatic pressure. The image is glomerular filtration barrier and Starling forces diagram.

steps.tx: **Tubuloglomerular feedback** operates via macula densa cells sensing sodium chloride delivery through apical NKCC2 cotransporters, releasing adenosine to constrict afferent arterioles and decrease GFR when distal tubular flow rises. The first step is Increased distal NaCl delivery. The next step is Macula densa NKCC2 sensing.

steps.tx: **Renal autoregulation** maintains renal blood flow and GFR relatively constant across mean arterial pressures ranging from 80 to 180 mmHg via myogenic tone and tubuloglomerular feedback. One side is Autoregulatory Range, and the other side is Outside Range. A key point is Mean arterial pressure 80 to 180 mmHg.

right.title: Outside Range
points: MAP below 80 leads to prerenal ischemia

steps.tx: The **proximal convoluted tubule** reabsorbs approximately 65% to 70% of filtered sodium and water, primarily coupled to sodium-hydrogen antiporter 3 (NHE3) and apical sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2). The paired value for Proximal tubule is NHE3 and SGLT2 cotransporter. The paired value for Thick ascending limb is NKCC2 symporter.

steps.tx: The **thick ascending limb** of Henle generates the medullary hyperosmolar gradient via the apical NKCC2 cotransporter without water reabsorption, establishing the countercurrent multiplier mechanism. The image is renal countercurrent multiplier mechanism in the loop of Henle. The lumen stays dilute because this segment is impermeable to water.

vis.caption: Medullary hyperosmolar gradient generation by the countercurrent multiplier (StewardMD).

steps.tx: The early **distal convoluted tubule** reabsorbs 5% to 7% of filtered sodium via the thiazide-sensitive sodium-chloride cotransporter NCC, while remaining impermeable to water. One side is Early Distal Tubule, and the other side is Physiological Consequence. Thiazides act here, so they waste sodium while the urine can still be concentrated.

steps.tx: **Cortical** collecting duct principal cells mediate electrogenic sodium reabsorption via epithelial sodium channels (ENaC) stimulated by aldosterone, creating a lumen-negative potential driving potassium and proton secretion. The first step is Aldosterone binds mineralocorticoid receptor. The next step is ENaC channels insert into apical membrane.

nodes.label: ENaC channels insert into apical membrane

steps.tx: **Free water clearance** is positive in diuresis when urine osmolality is lower than plasma osmolality, and negative during antidiuresis mediated by arginine vasopressin-induced aquaporin-2 translocation to principal cell apical membranes. One side is Water Diuresis, and the other side is Antidiuresis.
